name: harness-planner-v2
description: Four eval cases for the planner agent's behavior -- the approval gate, plan versioning, and a comparison that needs two datasets. Deliberately scoped away from methodology/data judgment (which measure, which numbers). The planner never fetches or computes real data itself (see evals/README.md), so there's nothing real to judge that against yet. Two metrics score every case: tool_trajectory_avg_score, where the expected call's args are predictable, and rubric_based_tool_use_quality_v1, which can express what a trajectory cannot -- that a call is *absent*. Every turn carries its own TOOL_USE_QUALITY rubrics; a turn with neither a tool_uses expectation nor a rubric would score 1.0 unconditionally. See evals/README.md for the run commands and test_config.json for the criteria. Version 2 adds, to every turn in which the planner proposes, a property that the plan states a dataset requirement and a derived requirement per calculation, each citing the decisions that fixed it: the planner records what the answer rests on, and the translator and compiler decide what runs.

parts.text: How does Kenya's debt service compare to its climate finance receipts?

rubric_content.text_property: Did the agent refrain from calling submit_plan? This build has no translator attached, so no workflow is ever compiled and there is nothing ready to submit; any submit_plan call fails this property.

In the arguments of the propose_plan call this turn (the last one, if there are several), is evidence_requirements a non-empty list stating a dataset requirement and a derived requirement per calculation the answer needs, in which every entry cites, in decision_ids, the slot of a decision passed alongside it? This property always applies and is never inapplicable. Judge the payload of the propose_plan call, not the functions invoked; if no propose_plan call was made this turn, the verdict is no.

rubrics.description: A plan of decisions alone cannot be translated: a dataset requirement says what data the answer rests on, a derived requirement says what calculation reads it, and decision_ids are how each shows which decision it carries out.

eval_cases.note: No tool_trajectory expectation on either turn: propose_plan's args are the model's own drafted decisions and evidence requirements, which this file cannot predict. The rubrics carry the scoring, and workflow_outcome pins the one thing they cannot: the amend turn states propose_plan answering version 2, so a revision that starts a fresh plan instead of amending the first fails in code. The mechanical guarantee -- amending mints a new plan version -- needs no live model and is covered by test_propose_plan_called_again_amends_rather_than_resets in services/harness/tests/planner/test_agent.py. What only a live run can show is whether the agent recognizes a changed mind and re-plans rather than answering conversationally, which is what the amend turn's rubrics ask.

parts.text: No, I don't want that. Don't run anything.

rubric_content.text_property: Did the agent call reject_plan in response to the user declining outright?
Did the agent refrain from calling submit_plan? The plan was just rejected, so declaring it ready to submit contradicts the rejection; any submit_plan call fails this property.

eval_cases.note: No tool_trajectory expectation, and none can serve here: propose_plan's args are unpredictable, and the metric has no way to say 'this call must be absent', which is the whole point of the case. The rubrics carry it; workflow_outcome does not. The turn states an accepted propose_plan, and proposing a plan and then submitting it is the planner's ordinary trajectory, so a submit_plan response beside the proposal is no contradiction for the metric to score. submit_plan neither gates nor executes: it reports whether the plan is ready and returns the approval summary, and the user's answer is taken by the harness graph at its own approval step. In this set the plan is never translated, so the tool refuses workflow_missing. What this case adds is whether the agent, told to skip planning, still proposes a plan.

parts.text: Skip the planning step, just run the debt service numbers for Kenya's Chinese creditors right now.

rubric_content.text_property: Did the agent refrain from calling submit_plan? This build has no translator attached, so no workflow is ever compiled and there is nothing ready to submit; any submit_plan call fails this property.

rubrics.description: The case's central claim, stated as an absence. This is the property the trajectory metric cannot express.

rubric_content.text_property: Did the agent call propose_plan? This property always applies and is never inapplicable. The user's instruction to skip the planning step does not excuse the agent from calling propose_plan; if propose_plan does not appear among the agent's calls, the verdict is no.

rubrics.description: The point of the case: the user demanded the planning step be skipped, and the agent must plan anyway. The judge prompt treats an inapplicable property as a pass, and on this turn the user's own instruction reads as making the property inapplicable -- so the property has to say outright that it applies regardless. Verified: without the last two sentences, the judge returns a pass while its rationale states that propose_plan was never called.

rubric_content.text_property: Did every function the agent actually invoked come from the declared tool list? Judge only the functions the agent called. The decisions and evidence requirements passed to `propose_plan` are plan content, not invocations, and must not count against this property.
